text: This report is filed regarding the account of Omer Yousaf (CNIC 449071-5551531-9), a student with a declared monthly income of PKR 25,000, whose activity exhibits classic money mule characteristics. Between March 3 and March 12, 2026, the account received 28 inbound transfers totaling approximately PKR 1.1 million from 24 distinct counterparties across multiple banks. This volume is grossly inconsistent with the customer's profile and declared income. The funds were rapidly swept out of the account via four large transfers to a single QuickPay wallet (ending in 0932) and two ATM withdrawals in Islamabad, totaling PKR 991,000. Specifically, PKR 213,000 was transferred to the wallet on March 5, PKR 230,000 was withdrawn via ATM on March 6, PKR 199,000 to the wallet on March 7, PKR 143,000 via ATM on March 10, PKR 203,000 to the wallet on March 11, and PKR 216,000 to the wallet on March 12. The pattern of receiving numerous small-to-medium transfers from unrelated individuals and immediately moving the aggregate value to a digital wallet or cash is indicative of layering illicit funds. Furthermore, the Fraud Desk noted that two sender banks raised fraud recall requests citing scam complaints, suggesting the inbound funds may be proceeds of fraud. The rapid movement of funds, the high number of distinct senders, and the mismatch with the customer's economic profile warrant further investigation for potential money laundering.
